claims.claim: **Usually self-limiting in immunocompetent children — symptomatic treatment only.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Short prodrome** (fever, lethargy, anorexia), then rash over 3–5 days: **crops of papules → vesicles → crusts**, usually fully crusted by 10 days.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surrounding erythema is normal**, especially as lesions crust — **cellulitis tends to be over-diagnosed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaccinated children can still get chickenpox, but it is typically mild**; the vaccine itself may cause a rash 1–3 weeks later.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Complications:** bacterial superinfection (especially *S. aureus* and GAS), encephalitis, pneumonia, arthritis, hepatitis, Reye syndrome — **more common in premature neonates, in neonates exposed when under 7 days old, in unimmunised adolescents and in the immunocompromised.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **At risk of complications:** malignancy · chemotherapy or high-dose steroids (prednisolone-equivalent over 20 mg/day for 2 weeks) · immunodeficiency.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infectious from 2 days before the rash until the vesicles crust.** Exposed children are potentially infectious from day 8 to 21 after exposure (8–28 if they received VZIG).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical diagnosis — no routine investigations.** In neonates or immunocompromised children a vesicle swab for VZV PCR may help.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunocompetent children over 1 week and under 12 years: no specific therapy.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid aspirin** (Reye syndrome) **and avoid NSAIDs** (invasive GAS).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Continue eczema treatment, including topical steroids.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider IV aciclovir for:** premature neonates and term neonates under 7 days of age · children at risk of, or with, complications.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider oral aciclovir for:** unvaccinated children over 12 years · severe eczema · chronic pulmonary disease · salicylate therapy · oral steroid therapy · secondary household cases (usually more severe).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exclude from school, kindergarten and childcare until all lesions have crusted.** Avoid admission where possible; if admitted, isolate with contact precautions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A pregnant woman exposed to chickenpox must be reviewed within 24 hours**, at any stage of pregnancy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contacts aged 1 month–1 year:** observe if not at risk; **consider VZIG if at risk of complications.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contacts over 1 year: give VZV vaccine within 5 days of exposure** if no contraindication; if they cannot be vaccinated and are at risk, consider VZIG. A second vaccine dose does no harm if status is uncertain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immunodeficient contacts should receive VZIG**; their susceptible household contacts should receive VZV vaccine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Term neonate under 1 week with a chickenpox-like rash: investigate and treat with IV aciclovir.** Any exposed neonate who becomes unwell starts IV aciclovir, **whether or not VZIG was given.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **VZIG for an infant whose mother's chickenpox starts in the window 7 days pre-delivery to 2 days post-delivery.** Maternal chickenpox, **born before 28 weeks** (no antibody transfer): VZIG. **Born after 28 weeks:** observe if maternal antibody present, VZIG if absent.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure under 1 week of age:** from the mother — assume no maternal antibody, give VZIG; from someone else — observe if maternal antibody present, VZIG if absent. **If maternal serology is unknown, assume antibodies absent.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Isolate an exposed hospitalised neonate for the first 21 days of life** (28 if VZIG given); exclude possibly exposed visitors from the nursery during days 8–21.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maternal varicella does not prevent breastfeeding**; cover any breast lesions with gauze and an occlusive dressing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VZIG IM by weight:** 0–10 kg 200 IU (1 vial) · 11–30 kg 400 IU (2 vials) · over 30 kg 600 IU (3 vials). This deliberately differs from the product information, to minimise wastage.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give VZIG within 96 hours of exposure** — it can still work up to 10 days. Normal human immunoglobulin can be used if VZIG is unavailable.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every child who meets criteria for IV aciclovir or VZIG with the paediatric team.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23
